model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), net debt zero, consolidated group, retention on marginal equity

inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 consolidated cash flow statement, 'Employee Stock Options/Units Expense' Rs 66.82 crore (KOTAKBANK.NS_Quarterly_Q4-2026.txt:256); H1 FY27 Rs 41.00 crore. Already expensed inside profit before tax; added back into the margin and charged through sbc_pct_path so it is deducted once.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-13T09:58:09Z (Yahoo regularMarketTime; NSE regular-session print, last trade before the weekend)
inputs.share_count_basis: 9,947.9m shares of Rs 1 face at 30-Sep-26 (paid-up capital Rs 994.79 crore, after the 5:1 split effective 14-Jan-2026) plus ~0.17% for in-the-money ESOPs/units (Q2 FY27 basic EPS 5.68 vs diluted 5.67) = ~9,965m. Held flat: ESOP cost is expensed in the flows.

book_value.note: Equity = capital + reserves at 30-Sep-26 (ESOP grants outstanding Rs 1,392m excluded, as in the CSV). TTM ROE on average of Sep-25 and Sep-26 equity.

inputs.wacc_rationale: Single INR cost of equity of 12.5% in all three scenarios; risk is charged once, through the scenario paths and weights. Same rate as ICICIBANK.NS, IBN and HDB so the India private banks compare directly. Built in the flows' own currency: India 10-year G-sec ~6.5% + beta ~0.85-0.9 x India total equity risk premium ~6.5-7.0% = ~12.3-12.6%. It is a cost of equity, not a WACC: the flow is after all funding costs. Terminal growth 6.5% nominal INR (6.0% bear).
inputs.lease_treatment: None separate. Indian GAAP: rent is an operating expense inside profit before tax; no lease liability on the balance sheet.
inputs.nci_treatment: None. Minority interest is nil (all subsidiaries wholly owned); share of associates' profit (Rs 1.07bn FY2026) is ignored in the margin, a ~0.5% understatement.
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank -> dcf-methods routing row 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker, thrift' (residual income on tangible book). Implemented as its algebraic equivalent, FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, the house precedent for banks (ICICIBANK.NS, IBN, HDB, USB, WFC). Deposits and borrowings are operating funding: net_debt, total_debt and cash are 0 by convention, not by measurement. BASIS: CONSOLIDATED group (bank + Kotak Life, Kotak Securities, AMC, Prime, Investments), because the Metrics.csv is consolidated; unlike ICICIBANK.NS (standalone + subsidiary bridge) there is no equity_bridge, the subsidiaries are in the flow. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = NET total income = total income - interest expended - policyholders' reserves/claims = Rs 107,563.70cr - 29,619.98cr - 20,088.76cr = Rs 57,854.96cr (Rs 578,550m) for FY2026 (KOTAKBANK.NS_Quarterly_Q4-2026.txt:26-31). The CSV 'Revenue' of Rs 1,075,637m is GROSS total income and is not the base. FY2025 on the same basis Rs 54,783.83cr (+5.6% in FY2026); H1 FY27 Rs 31,425.51cr vs Rs 27,753.58cr (+13.2%; +10.5% excluding the 'profit on sale of investments incl. insurance revaluation' line). 'ebitda' = profit before tax ex exceptional + ESOP cost: FY2026 (25,992.72 - 367.79 Infina gain + 66.82) / 57,854.96 = 44.41%; H1 FY27 PBT 15,039.16cr = 47.86%. da 0 (depreciation is inside PBT; branch/IT capex ~Rs 10.6bn treated as funded within it). Tax 26.2% FY2026, 26.05% H1 FY27 -> 26.0%. 'capex' = equity retained to fund growth = k x g/(1+g), k = marginal equity per rupee of net total income. Actual k is 3.13 (equity Rs 1,811,128m / Rs 578,550m at 31-Mar-26; 3.16 on Sep-26 equity over TTM income), which reflects standalone CET-1 of 21.34% and capital adequacy of 21.86% at Sep-26, far above the ~8-9% CET-1 minimum. At actual k and TTM ROE of 11.8%, 12%+ growth would absorb all earnings, which is in fact what happens (payout ~3%: FY2026 dividend Rs 0.65/share, Rs 6.47bn paid in H1 FY27) while the ratio drifts down as loans outgrow equity. So NEW growth is capitalised at k = 2.40 base (~16% CET-1, where ICICI runs), 2.15 bull, 2.80 bear; the existing surplus is neither released as a special dividend nor compounded, and is valued only through the income it already earns. last_fcf = FY2026 model-basis FCFE: profit ex the Infina gain ~Rs 190.2bn less 2.40 x the FY2026 increase in net total income (Rs 30.7bn) = ~Rs 116.5bn; it is high relative to year 1 because FY2026 income growth was only 5.6%. Cash actually distributed was Rs 4.97bn. reported_fcf = FY2026 consolidated net profit (the CSV FreeCashFlow of Rs 406,686m is deposit-flow noise). CROSS-CHECK: base value is ~1.1-1.2x tangible book of Rs 194/share, which is what residual income gives for a bank earning 12-14% on equity against a 12.5% cost of equity; the market pays ~2.5x book and ~22.6x TTM EPS of Rs 21.6. DATA GAPS: NIM and CASA are not in the downloaded results filings; consolidated CET-1 not located (standalone used). Price is a regular-session print, not after-hours.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: below equity_5yr_cagr (16.5%) and near eps_5yr_cagr (13.9%); year-1 net total income growth anchored on H1 FY27
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3-yr CAGR 17.5% vs EPS 3-yr CAGR 9.0% diverge by more than 30%: book has compounded faster than earnings because almost nothing is paid out and FY2025 booked a Rs 38bn one-off gain (Zurich Kotak General Insurance stake sale), so ROE has slid from ~14-15% to ~11.8% TTM. Equity CAGR overstates sustainable earnings growth.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue CAGRs are on GROSS total income (CSV Revenue), FY2026 vs FY2023/FY2021. 'FCF' CAGRs use consolidated net profit as the owner-flow proxy because bank FCF is deposit noise; SBC is ~0.1% of income and does not distort it. FY2026 EPS (19.39) fell from FY2025 (22.26) only because of the FY2025 one-off gain.

base.capex_rationale: Equity retention = 240 x g/(1+g) percent of net total income: marginal equity / net total income 2.40 vs 3.13 actual at 31-Mar-26 (about 16% CET-1 on new growth vs 21.3% standalone today).
base.narrative: Net total income grows 12.5% in FY2027 (H1 FY27 +13.2% reported, +10.5% excluding investment/revaluation gains, with advances +21.9% and deposits +23.4% YoY at 30-Sep-26 feeding H2), 13% for two years as the larger book earns through, then fades to 7% by year 10 and 6.5% nominal INR thereafter. Pre-tax margin settles at 46% of net total income (FY2026 44.3% ex the Infina gain, H1 FY27 47.9% helped by treasury gains and lower provisions). Each rupee of income growth is backed by Rs 2.40 of new equity (about 16% CET-1 against 21% today), a marginal ROE near 14%; the existing capital surplus is neither released nor grown.

bull.capex_rationale: Equity retention = 215 x g/(1+g) percent of net total income (about 14.5% CET-1 on new growth).
bull.narrative: Loan growth stays near 20% for longer and the deposit franchise funds it without margin loss: income growth 14-15% for four years fading to 7.5%. Pre-tax margin rises to 49% as credit costs on unsecured retail normalise and operating leverage comes through. New growth is capitalised at Rs 2.15 of equity per rupee of income (about 14.5% CET-1), a marginal ROE near 17%. No release of the existing surplus is assumed even here.

bear.capex_rationale: Equity retention = 280 x g/(1+g) percent of net total income (about 19% CET-1 on new growth; surplus capital stays idle).
bear.narrative: Rate cuts compress the margin faster than deposits reprice, the 22% loan growth of the past year seasons badly, and growth slows to 10% then 6%. Pre-tax margin falls to 42% (below FY2026's 44.3%, a year that already carried elevated unsecured-retail and microfinance provisions). The bank keeps running at today's capital intensity: Rs 2.80 of equity per rupee of new income (about 19% CET-1), a marginal ROE near 11%, below the cost of equity, so growth destroys value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 20/50/30, the same as ICICIBANK.NS so the two compare directly, against a house default of 15/50/35. Bear is above 15% because loans grew ~22% in the year to Sep-26 into an easing cycle (the growth that precedes both margin compression and credit seasoning) and because NIM/CASA could not be checked from the filings held. Bull is below 35% because it needs both a higher margin and leaner capital, and management has run 20%+ CET-1 for six years.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Kotak is a high-quality, very over-capitalised bank earning ~12% on equity. At a 12.5% INR cost of equity a 12-14% ROE is worth a little over book, not the ~2.5x the market pays; the gap is the market using a far lower discount rate and assuming the capital surplus is eventually levered or returned. The model gives credit for leaner capital on new growth only.
key_risks_to_valuation: Capital intensity is the swing factor: every 0.1 change in marginal equity per rupee of income moves value several percent; a credible plan to run at ~15% CET-1 or return the surplus would lift the value materially
Cost of equity: at 11% rather than 12.5% the base value rises by roughly a third; the market price implies single-digit
Consolidated flow embeds Kotak Life, Securities and AMC at the group margin; a sum-of-parts at listed-peer multiples would be higher
NIM and CASA are not observed in the filings held, so the margin path rests on reported PBT only
FY2027 H1 margin flattered by investment gains and low provisions
